title: Negative (toward C:contained-swimmers): the layered wave-pinning crawlers from noise never divide; raising contractility rho* from 0.2 to 0.25 keeps crawlers that only merge, and 0.3-0.35 freezes every cell as a static layered disk
summary: World: research/alife/collective/contrib/20261026T0406-c31-crawlers-from-noise-claim/world.py (layer made by the polarity protein, excluded cargo, random-field start), varying rho* (the contractility threshold), snap.py to t=14. rho*=0.25 (seeds 0, 1): as at 0.2, 31-33 random domains leave 6-7 round cells, the larger ones polarize and crawl, and crawlers absorb static cells, so bodies fall 7 -> 2 and 6 -> 1 by t=14 with no fission (div_rs0.25_s*.png). rho*=0.3 and 0.35 (seed 0): 8 and 7 round cells with uniformly high rho and intact s rings form by t~2.3 and then nothing changes to t=14: no symmetry breaking, no motion, no merging, no division (div_rs0.3.png, div_rs0.35.png). So in this world the crawling window is rho* <= ~0.25, and on neither side of it does a cell divide: the polarity's winner-take-all competition through the shared per-body pool keeps one front per cell, and large crawlers grow by absorbing others. Division for C:contained-swimmers needs an added mechanism (a size-triggered instability or growth-driven fission as in c04's crawler), not a contractility change.

finding.operator: contractility threshold rho* in the layered wave-pinning crawler from noise
finding.control: rho* = 0.25 (2 seeds), 0.3, 0.35 (1 seed each) against 0.2 (the claim's 3 seeds)
finding.result: 0 divisions in all runs; rho* 0.25: bodies 7->2 and 6->1 by merging; rho* 0.3/0.35: 8 and 7 static disks, no change after t~2.3
